description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol allows privileged clients such as dock or taskbar
components to observe and manage toplevel windows on behalf of the
compositor. It provides access to window metadata (title, app-id,
state, parent, outputs), allows requests to maximize, minimize,
activate, close, or fullscreen a toplevel, and supports a dock
preview context for thumbnail or list display and tooltip overlays.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", "may", and "recommended"
in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
description.summary: manage foreign toplevel windows

description.text:
A singleton global that emits one treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3
object per mapped toplevel window. Clients bind this global to
receive the toplevel event stream and to create dock preview
contexts.

A toplevel is defined as a surface with a role similar to
xdg_toplevel. XWayland surfaces may be treated like toplevels
in this protocol.

Clients which only care about the current state can perform a
roundtrip after binding this global.

The typical lifecycle is:
1. Client binds treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v3.
2. Compositor emits a toplevel event for each already-mapped
toplevel, followed by individual property events and a done
event on each handle.
3. As windows appear and disappear the compositor emits further
toplevel events and closed events on the corresponding handles.
4. When the client no longer needs the manager it sends stop,
waits for the finished event, destroys the handles, and then
the manager itself. Outstanding handles remain usable until
the client destroys them individually.
description.summary: observe and manage toplevel windows

description.text:
This request should be called either when the client will no
longer use the manager, or after the finished event has been
received.

If a client wishes to destroy this object it should send a
stop request and wait for a finished event, then destroy the
handles and then this object.

Existing treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 objects created
through this manager are not affected and must be destroyed
separately by the client.
description.summary: destroy the manager object

description.text:
This request indicates that the client no longer wishes to
receive events for new toplevels.

The Wayland protocol is asynchronous, meaning the compositor
may send further toplevel events until the stop request is
processed. The client should wait for a finished event
before destroying this object.
description.summary: stop sending events

description.text:
Create a treeland_dock_preview_context_v3 associated with the
given surface. The surface must be a valid wl_surface owned by
the calling client and serves as the anchor for all preview
and tooltip positioning.

Only one dock preview context may be active per surface at a
time. If the surface already has an active context, the client
must destroy it via treeland_dock_preview_context_v3.destroy
before creating a new one; otherwise the compositor raises the
context_already_exists protocol error and does not create the
requested object.
description.summary: create a dock preview context for a surface

args.name: relative_surface
args.summary: anchor surface for preview and tooltip positioning

args.name: id
args.summary: the new dock preview context object

description.text:
Emitted by the compositor whenever a new toplevel window is
mapped. The event is sent for all toplevels regardless of
which application created them.

Immediately after this event the compositor will send the
initial property events (title, app_id, pid, identifier,
state, output_enter, parent, and so on) on the new handle,
followed by a done event. The client should treat all
property events received before the first done as the
initial snapshot.
description.summary: a toplevel window has been mapped

args.name: toplevel
args.summary: the new toplevel handle

description.text:
This event indicates that the compositor is done sending
events to this object. The client should destroy the object.
See treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v3.destroy for more
information.

The compositor must not send any more toplevel events after
this event.

Outstanding treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 objects are
not affected by this event.
description.summary: the compositor has finished with the toplevel manager

description.text:
Error values raised as protocol errors on misuse of
treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v3 requests.
description.summary: protocol errors for this interface

entries.name: invalid_surface
entries.summary: the relative_surface passed to get_dock_preview_context is not a valid wl_surface owned by the calling client

entries.name: context_already_exists
entries.summary: get_dock_preview_context was called for a surface that already has an active dock preview context; the client must destroy the existing context first

description.text:
Represents a single mapped toplevel window. The compositor
creates this object in response to the manager's toplevel event
and destroys the server-side resource when the window is
unmapped (signalled by the closed event).

After the compositor sends closed, the client must not send
any requests other than destroy. The client should call destroy
promptly after receiving closed to release compositor-side
tracking state.

All property events (title, app_id, pid, identifier,
output_enter, output_leave, state, parent) are grouped by a
trailing done event so that a batch of related changes appears
atomic to the client.
description.summary: handle for a foreign toplevel window

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 object and
release all associated client-side resources.

This request may be sent at any time, including before the
compositor sends the closed event. When sent after closed,
it finalizes the destruction sequence initiated by the
compositor. When sent before closed, the compositor will
silently drop any further events for this handle.

When a handle is destroyed, a new handle may not be created
by the compositor until the toplevel is unmapped and then
remapped. Destroying a toplevel handle is not recommended
unless the client is cleaning up child objects before
destroying the manager, the toplevel was closed, or the
handle will not be used in the future.

Other protocols which extend the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 interface should
require destructors for extension interfaces to be called
before allowing the toplevel handle to be destroyed.
description.summary: destroy the handle object

description.text:
Request that the compositor maximize the toplevel. The
compositor may ignore the request. If the maximized state
changes, the compositor will reflect this in a subsequent
state event followed by done.
description.summary: request that the toplevel be maximized

description.text:
Request that the compositor restore the toplevel from the
maximized state. The compositor may ignore the request. If
the state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.
description.summary: request that the toplevel be unmaximized

description.text:
Request that the compositor minimize the toplevel. The
compositor may ignore the request. If the minimized state
changes, the compositor will reflect this in a subsequent
state event followed by done.
description.summary: request that the toplevel be minimized

description.text:
Request that the compositor restore the toplevel from the
minimized state. The compositor may ignore the request. If
the state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.
description.summary: request that the toplevel be unminimized

description.text:
Request that the compositor fullscreen the toplevel on the
given output. If output is null, the compositor chooses the
output. The output argument is a hint only; the compositor
may fullscreen on a different output or not at all.

If the fullscreen state or visible outputs change, the
compositor will reflect this via state and output_enter /
output_leave events followed by done.
description.summary: request that the toplevel enter fullscreen

args.name: output
args.summary: preferred output for fullscreen, or null for compositor choice

description.text:
Request that the compositor exit the fullscreen state for
the toplevel. The compositor may ignore the request. If the
state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.
description.summary: request that the toplevel leave fullscreen

description.text:
Request that the compositor give keyboard focus to the
toplevel on the given seat. There is no guarantee the
toplevel will actually be activated; the compositor may
ignore the request based on seat focus policy or security
considerations.
description.summary: request that the toplevel be activated

args.name: seat
args.summary: the seat on which to activate the toplevel

description.text:
Send a close request to the toplevel. The compositor
typically forwards this to the application using a
shell-specific mechanism such as xdg_toplevel.close.
There is no guarantee the application will honour the
request. If the toplevel is eventually unmapped, the
compositor will emit the closed event on this handle.
description.summary: request that the toplevel close itself

description.text:
Inform the compositor of the rectangle on surface that
visually represents this toplevel (for example the taskbar
icon or thumbnail), similar to the EWMH
_NET_WM_ICON_GEOMETRY property. The compositor may use this
as a hint for minimize animations or similar effects.

The client is not required to set this geometry. If unset,
the compositor applies an implementation-defined default.
If the client sets multiple rectangles, only the last one
takes effect.

Coordinates are in surface-local space of the given surface.
Setting width = height = 0 removes a previously set geometry.

The compositor raises the invalid_geometry error if the
provided dimensions are otherwise out of range.
description.summary: set the icon geometry of the toplevel

args.name: surface
args.summary: surface that contains the visual representation

args.name: x
args.summary: x offset in surface-local coordinates

args.name: y
args.summary: y offset in surface-local coordinates

args.name: width
args.summary: width of the rectangle in surface-local coordinates

args.name: height
args.summary: height of the rectangle in surface-local coordinates

description.text:
Emitted by the compositor when it knows the process ID of
the application that owns this toplevel. This event is sent
once as part of the initial property snapshot, before the
first done event, and is not re-sent unless the owning
process changes.
description.summary: process ID of the owning application

args.name: pid
args.summary: process ID of the application

description.text:
Emitted whenever the title of the toplevel changes. The
initial title is sent as part of the snapshot before the
first done event.
description.summary: toplevel title has changed

args.name: title
args.summary: the current title of the toplevel

description.text:
Emitted whenever the app-id of the toplevel changes. The
initial app-id is sent as part of the snapshot before the
first done event.
description.summary: toplevel app-id has changed

args.name: app_id
args.summary: the current application ID of the toplevel

description.text:
This identifier is used to check if two or more toplevel
handles belong to the same toplevel.

The identifier is useful for command line tools or
privileged clients which may need to reference an exact
toplevel across processes or instances of the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v3 global.

The compositor sends this event exactly once, when the
handle is created, as part of the initial property
snapshot.

The identifier must be unique per toplevel and its
handles. Two different toplevels must not have the same
identifier. The identifier is only valid as long as the
toplevel is mapped. If the toplevel is unmapped the
identifier must not be reused. An identifier must not be
reused by the compositor to ensure there are no races when
sharing identifiers between processes.
description.summary: a stable identifier for a toplevel

args.name: identifier
args.summary: unique stable identifier for this toplevel

description.text:
Emitted when the toplevel becomes visible on the given
output. A toplevel may be visible on multiple outputs
simultaneously. This event is sent as part of the initial
snapshot and whenever the set of visible outputs changes.
description.summary: toplevel is now visible on an output

args.name: output
args.summary: the output the toplevel entered

description.text:
Emitted when the toplevel stops being visible on the given
output. A corresponding output_enter event for the same
output is guaranteed to have been sent before this event.
description.summary: toplevel is no longer visible on an output

args.name: output
args.summary: the output the toplevel left

description.text:
Emitted immediately after the handle is created as part of
the initial property snapshot, and again each time the
toplevel state changes due to a compositor action or a
client request on this protocol.

The state argument is an array of uint32 values, each
corresponding to an entry in the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3.state
enum. An entry is present in the array when the corresponding
state is active.
description.summary: toplevel state has changed

args.name: state
args.summary: array of active treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3.state enum values encoded as uint32

description.text:
Emitted after the compositor has sent all property events for
the current atomic update batch (title, app_id, pid,
identifier, state, output_enter, output_leave, parent). The
client should process the preceding events as a single
coherent state snapshot only upon receiving done.

This allows changes to the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 properties to be
atomically applied. Other protocols which extend the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 interface may use this
event to also atomically apply any pending state.

This event must not be sent after the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3.closed event.
description.summary: all pending property changes have been sent

description.text:
Emitted when the toplevel is unmapped or destroyed by the
compositor. No further property events will be sent on this
handle after closed. The handle becomes inert; the client
must not send any requests except destroy, which it should
call promptly to release compositor-side tracking resources.

Other protocols which extend the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 interface must also
ignore requests other than their destructors.
description.summary: the toplevel window has been unmapped

description.text:
Emitted whenever the parent-child relationship of this
toplevel changes. The parent arg is null when the toplevel
has no parent (i.e. it is a top-level root window).

This event is not re-sent when the client destroys the
parent handle; the relationship on the compositor side is
unchanged by client-side destruction of the parent object.
description.summary: parent toplevel has changed

args.name: parent
args.summary: the parent toplevel handle, or null if there is no parent

description.text:
Flags that describe the current state of a toplevel window.
These correspond to the states with the same names defined
in the xdg-toplevel interface. Each flag is encoded as a
uint32 value in the array sent by the state event.
description.summary: toplevel window state flags

entries.name: attention
entries.summary: the toplevel is requesting user attention

description.text:
Error values raised as protocol errors on misuse of
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3 requests.
description.summary: protocol errors for this interface

entries.name: invalid_geometry
entries.summary: the provided set_icon_geometry dimensions are invalid

description.text:
Provides the dock or taskbar component with the ability to
display a thumbnail preview of one or more toplevels and to
show a client-drawn tooltip surface, both positioned relative
to the anchor surface supplied to get_dock_preview_context.

The object is created by
treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v3.get_dock_preview_context
and is valid until the client calls destroy. The compositor
emits enter and leave events when the pointer enters or leaves
the active preview area.

The preview and the tooltip share one popover slot: showing
either one replaces whatever the context displayed before.

Version 2 adds the show_list request, which shows the same
preview as show but asks for a vertical list of rows instead
of thumbnails. show keeps its thumbnail meaning in both
versions.
description.summary: dock preview and tooltip context for a surface

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_dock_preview_context_v3 object and
release all associated compositor resources. Any visible
preview or tooltip is hidden immediately. After this request
the compositor will no longer send any event.
description.summary: destroy the dock preview context

description.text:
Request that the compositor display thumbnail previews for
the toplevels identified by the identifiers array. The popup
is positioned at (x, y) in the coordinate space of the
anchor surface supplied at context creation, on the side
indicated by direction.

This request always asks for the thumbnail presentation.
A client that wants the list presentation sends show_list
instead, which takes the same arguments.

The identifiers argument is a wl_array of uint32 identifier
values, each matching the identifier sent by the
treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v3.identifier event. The
compositor ignores identifiers that do not correspond to a
currently mapped toplevel.

Calling show while a preview is already visible replaces
the previous content atomically. If a tooltip is visible,
the preview replaces it as well: the tooltip is hidden.
description.summary: show a thumbnail preview of the given toplevels

args.name: identifiers
args.summary: array of uint32 toplevel identifiers to preview

args.name: x
args.summary: x offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: y
args.summary: y offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: direction
args.summary: which side of the anchor surface the preview appears on

description.text:
Display the given surface as the tooltip of this context, at
(x, y) in the coordinate space of the anchor surface and on
the side indicated by direction. The compositor computes the
final position from these values and may move the tooltip to
keep it on the output; clients must not assume the request is
honored exactly. Any tooltip this context displayed before is
replaced.

The compositor draws its popover frame (tint, border,
shadow) exactly behind the surface and uses the surface's
committed logical size as the tooltip size. There is no
extra padding on any side: the client is responsible for
its own inner padding and for keeping its content inside
the rounded corners. The client provides content only and
must not draw its own popover background, otherwise it
covers the frame the compositor draws.

The surface must already have a committed buffer when this
request is sent. A surface without content is a client
error: the compositor shows nothing for that request. Asking
for a surface that is already shown, with the same or a new
position, is allowed and needs no further commit; commits
after the tooltip is shown update its content.

A request for a surface other than the one this context
already shows replaces the tooltip, and the compositor may
animate the switch, shrinking and fading out the replaced
tooltip into the new one. Showing the surface this context
already shows is not a replacement: the compositor keeps
drawing that one surface, moved to the new position, and
plays no animation, even when the surface committed
different content in the meantime. A client that wants a
transition between two tooltips therefore has to put them
on separate surfaces; one surface repainted in place
changes the tooltip without animating.

This request assigns a compositor-side role to the surface,
so the surface must be owned by the calling client and must
not have any other role yet; the anchor surface of this
context cannot be used either. Otherwise the compositor
raises invalid_surface. The role is never released: once a
surface has been shown as a tooltip it can only be shown as
a tooltip again. The compositor does not scale the tooltip;
if it does not fit on the output it may be clipped.

The surface receives no pointer or keyboard input, no focus
and no activation. It is owned by the client: the
compositor only stops using it and never destroys it.
description.summary: show a client-drawn tooltip surface

args.name: surface
args.summary: the wl_surface to display as the tooltip content

args.name: x
args.summary: x offset of the tooltip in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: y
args.summary: y offset of the tooltip in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: direction
args.summary: which side of the anchor surface the tooltip appears on

description.text:
Request that the compositor hide the currently visible
popover, that is the preview popup and the tooltip surface
alike. If nothing is visible this request is a no-op.

A hidden tooltip is not destroyed and keeps the role of its
surface; the client shows it again with another
show_tooltip_surface request.
description.summary: hide the popover

description.text:
Behaves exactly like show, except that the compositor
presents the toplevels as a vertical list of rows, one row
per toplevel, instead of thumbnails side by side.

The arguments and the popup placement are the same as show,
and the two requests replace each other exactly like two
calls of show do.
description.summary: show a list preview of the given toplevels

args.name: identifiers
args.summary: array of uint32 toplevel identifiers to preview

args.name: x
args.summary: x offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: y
args.summary: y offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

args.name: direction
args.summary: which side of the anchor surface the preview appears on

description.text:
Emitted when the pointer device enters the active preview
popup area managed by this context. The compositor sends
this event only while a preview is visible (i.e. after
show and before close or destroy).
description.summary: pointer entered the preview area

description.text:
Emitted when the pointer device leaves the active preview
popup area managed by this context. A corresponding enter
event is guaranteed to have been sent before this event.
description.summary: pointer left the preview area

description.text:
Error values raised as protocol errors on misuse of
treeland_dock_preview_context_v3 requests.
description.summary: protocol errors for this interface

entries.name: invalid_surface
entries.summary: the wl_surface is not owned by this client, has another role, or is the anchor surface

description.text:
Specifies on which side of the anchor surface the preview
popup or tooltip should appear. The compositor uses this
value as a placement hint; it may choose a different side
if the requested side would be clipped by the screen edge.
description.summary: position of the preview relative to the anchor surface

entries.name: top
entries.summary: preview appears above the anchor surface

entries.name: right
entries.summary: preview appears to the right of the anchor surface

entries.name: bottom
entries.summary: preview appears below the anchor surface

entries.name: left
entries.summary: preview appears to the left of the anchor surface
